newsitem.title: INDIA: IMF aide sees $230 bln in emerging markets in 1997.
newsitem.headline: IMF aide sees $230 bln in emerging markets in 1997.

text.p: Capital flows into emerging markets is estimated to total around $230 billion in 1997, the same level as in 1996, a senior official of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday.

"Last year, in 1996, $230 billion of capital flowed into emerging markets out of which India got just $4.0 billion. In 1997, a similar amount of $230 billion is expected to flow into emerging markets," M.R.Sivaraman, IMF executive director, told reporters in New Delhi.
"Brazil alone is expected to get $25-30 billion in 1997," Sivaraman said.
The bulk of the capital flows into emerging markets in 1996 were in the form of equity investment, he added.
India should get more than $4.0 billion of capital inflows in 1997, Sivaraman said, without elaborating.
